author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The University of Rhode Island celebrated the opening of its renovated Fine Arts Center on Monday with a ribbon-cutting ceremony in Kingston, NBC 10 reported.
University leaders, students, elected officials and community members gathered outside the Robert E. Will Theatre on the Kingston campus. An open house and guided tours followed the ceremony.

The $99 million project included renovations to the 58-year-old Fine Arts Center and construction of a new 71,000-square-foot, three-story academic building. The expansion includes a theater lobby, an art gallery and classrooms.

New spaces are dedicated to digital art and media, while recording studios and other rooms support artists, designers, composers, performers and scholars. The building is open for classes this semester.

The project was paid for through state capital funds, university funding and a bond approved by Rhode Island voters in 2021. URI also dedicated a choral room to the late Rhode Island Senate President Dominick J. Ruggerio.
dek: A ribbon-cutting marked the opening of a renovated arts facility and a new three-story academic building on Monday.
headline: URI opens $99 million Fine Arts Center renovation in Kingston
